Warrior.description: Master of arms. Onslaught proc on every hit.
Warrior.flavor: You don't need a new name. The old one was enough.

Paladin.description: Holy warrior. Holy Smite proc vs undead. Heals on kill.
Paladin.flavor: Aerthis acknowledges your oath. The flame at the Shrine burns white-blue.

Shadowknight.description: Dark blade. Harm Touch proc. Drains life on every hit.
Shadowknight.flavor: Morvenna is watching. The flame at the Shrine burns amber-black.

Ranger.description: Seasoned tracker. True Shot proc on every hit. +1 daily hunt.
Ranger.flavor: The forest doesn't change. You do. That's the difference.

Hunter.description: Predator proc on every hit. Extended crit range.
Hunter.flavor: The forest edge accepts you as part of its pattern. Something shifts.

Warden.description: Forest Fury proc on hit. Hard to kill — strong defense.
Warden.flavor: Thornax approves. The Whisperwood breathes with you.

Mage.description: Pure arcane focus. Arcane Surge proc on hit.
Mage.flavor: The resonance hums louder now. You've always known. You just listen better.

Wizard.description: INT drives all attack rolls. Arcane Nova proc (1d10).
Wizard.flavor: Sylvara tears open the door for you. The resonance sings aloud.

Necromancer.description: Death Touch proc vs undead. Deep attunement to the dead.
Necromancer.flavor: Morvenna welcomes your final lesson. The Shrine goes dead quiet.

Rogue.description: Survivor. Backstab proc on every hit.
Rogue.flavor: You've survived this long without a title. That IS the title.

Shadowblade.description: Shadow Strike proc on every hit. Crits on 17+.
Shadowblade.flavor: The knife feels lighter. The dark feels familiar in a way it didn't before.

Trickster.description: Lucky Break proc on hit. Gold mastery. Gambling advantage.
Trickster.flavor: A courier-sprite winks at you from a dark corner of the Stone Hearth. You don't question it.

Cleric.description: Devoted healer. Undead Bane proc. Enhanced consumable healing.
Cleric.flavor: The flame doesn't change. But it burns a little steadier when you're near.

High Priest.description: WIS drives attack rolls. Divine Touch proc — heals 25 HP on proc.
High Priest.flavor: The flame at the Shrine burns three times as bright for a moment. Then settles.

Shaman.description: Spirit Wrath proc on hit. Forest XP bonus. Passive heal on forest events.
Shaman.flavor: The Whisperwood acknowledges you as something more than a visitor. That distinction matters.

aerthis.name: Aerthis
aerthis.title: The Unbending
aerthis.symbol: A balanced scale, one side holding flame
aerthis.shrine_flavor: The flame at the Shrine burns white-blue when Aerthis is acknowledged.
npc_topics: Aerthis does not reward the devout for faith. He rewards them for action. There's a distinction.
A Paladin's oath to Aerthis is not symbolic. The god hears every word.
Aerthis and Sylvara have not spoken since the Sundering. Neither will say why.
The Shrine was Aerthis's first. The other gods arrived later, as guests.
aerthis.monster_connection: Undead are anathema to Aerthis — his priests are compelled to destroy them.
aerthis.desc: God of Order, law, and unwavering light. Patron of Clerics and Paladins.

sylvara.name: Sylvara
sylvara.title: The Unbound
sylvara.symbol: A broken circle with lightning across the gap
sylvara.shrine_flavor: The flame stutters and forks when Sylvara's power moves through an area.
npc_topics: Sylvara doesn't grant power. She tears open the door to it and steps aside.
The gap between an Apprentice and a Wizard is the moment they stopped asking permission from the rules.
Necromancy is Sylvara's gift misunderstood. Death is change. She sees no difference.
Aeridor's mages served Sylvara, at the end. That's one theory for why it ended the way it did.
sylvara.monster_connection: Magic constructs and resonance entities are touched by her domain.
sylvara.desc: Goddess of chaos, raw magic, and change. Patron of Mages and Wizards.

thornax.name: Thornax
thornax.title: The Patient
thornax.symbol: Three roots coiled into a spiral
thornax.shrine_flavor: The Whisperwood is Thornax's expression. The forest has opinions, and they are his.
npc_topics: Thornax doesn't answer prayers. He answers behavior. Prove you belong, and the forest opens.
The Whisperwood is not a place Thornax made. It is a part of him that became too large to contain.
Rangers pray to Thornax before the first hunt of a season. Not for luck. For permission.
The Silvani call him by a different name. They say ours is a child's word for something older.
thornax.monster_connection: The elder treants and deep forest creatures are his to command.
thornax.desc: God of balance, nature, and cycles. Patron of Rangers, Wardens, and Shamans.

morvenna.name: Morvenna
morvenna.title: The Inevitable
morvenna.symbol: A moth above a candle flame
morvenna.shrine_flavor: The flame burns amber-black on Morvenna's feast night. Elara calls it a warning. The Hooded Figure calls it an invitation.
epithets: She Who Waits at the Door
npc_topics: Morvenna doesn't want worship. She wants witnesses. Someone to see what death really is.
A Shadowknight serves Morvenna not because they fear death, but because they've stopped.
Necromancy isn't defying death. It's reading her handwriting aloud.
On Morvenna's Eve, she walks Aethelgard like anyone else. She says she just wants to see how it's going.
morvenna.monster_connection: The undead are her soldiers, her failed experiments, and sometimes her messengers.
morvenna.desc: Goddess of death, transformation, and endings. Patron of Shadowknights and Necromancers.

vethran.name: Vethran
vethran.title: The Blade Forged
vethran.symbol: A greatsword driven into an anvil
vethran.shrine_flavor: There is no shrine to Vethran in Oakhaven. Warriors carve his mark into their weapons instead.
npc_topics: Vethran has no church. He has veterans.
A warrior who survives enough battles stops praying and starts being answered.
Vethran doesn't distinguish between a soldier and a mercenary. He only distinguishes between those who held and those who ran.
Hemlock keeps a chip of iron behind the counter. Old custom. Vethran's domain, gold's domain — both about value held in the hand.
vethran.monster_connection: None specific — Vethran claims the fallen of all sides.
vethran.desc: God of war, honor, and the blade. Patron of Warriors.

corvus.name: Corvus
corvus.title: The Laughing Road
corvus.symbol: A coin balanced on its edge
corvus.shrine_flavor: Corvus has no shrine. He has back rooms, loose floorboards, and the pause before someone laughs.
npc_topics: Corvus blesses no one. He arranges circumstances. What you do with them is your prayer.
Every caravan runner carries his mark. Not faith — insurance. He's the one who knows where all the roads lead.
Rogues call him the Patron of Favorable Odds. He would say that's an overcompliment. He just likes being in the room.
The Hooded Figure paid in Corvus coins once. Nobody knows what that means.
corvus.monster_connection: Corvus claims no monsters — only the people who made poor choices near them.
corvus.desc: God of travelers, merchants, trickery, and luck. Patron of Rogues and Tricksters.
